CHAPTER 11  Food and Nutrient Delivery
percentage of the daily value (DV) supplied by a serving, show-
ing how a product fits into an overall diet by comparing its 
nutrient content with recommended intakes of those nutrients 
(Table 11-3). DVs are not recommended intakes for individuals; 
they are simply reference points to provide some perspective 
on daily nutrient needs and are based on a 2000-kcal diet. For 
example, individuals who consume diets supplying more or 
fewer calories can still use the DVs as a rough guide to ensure 
that they are getting adequate amounts of vitamin C, for 
example, but not too much saturated fat.
The DVs are listed for nutrients for which RDAs already exist 
(in which case they are known as reference daily intakes [RDIs]) 
(Table 11-4) and for which no RDAs exist (in which case they are
